answers.why: the absence of the operator's decision, said as an absence: a wiring that names nothing is not a reader that reads nothing. It is also the only absence the board may write back
a name the caravan has no facts for: the block says it does not know, which is not the same as knowing it cannot
the defect the rule exists for: the name says vision, the facts say `text`. The promise is read from `ModelKind`, never from the name
an absence of a promise, kept apart from a promise that says no: the block cannot say 'cannot' for a model that never said anything
the only answer that is not an absence, and the only one the block says as a promise rather than as a hole

the word the block has no key for, and the absence is named rather than drawn as a key it would never use: `itself` answers where a pool is named, and the board's row names no pool, so this word cannot come from the board. It is asked here with a request's pool, which is where the rule can answer it

the negative case, and the one the program cannot run: no facts answer this word, so it is the word the table has no key for. A page that names a state the rule does not have is the fact read a second way; what the block does with such a word — say it as the program says it — is pinned by scripts/test_js_reader_block.py

row.why: the absence of the operator's decision is said in words, not drawn as an empty field: an empty field next to a state word reads as a reader that reads nothing
the row says two facts, not one: the name the board named, and the answer the rule gave for it
the case the rule exists for, seen from the page: a name that says vision and facts that say `text`. The state on the row is the answer, not the name
a model with no named inputs is not a model that refused the word
the same name as two cases above, answered as an absence of facts — which is why the block cannot work the state out from the name: the same string gives three answers

the negative case for the row: an answer the table has no word for is still shown as the program says it — the row does not fall back to 'nothing' or to a guess, which would be a state invented on the page

key.why: the cable key, said once in `ReaderBlock.key()`: one board has one reader, so the key is the block's prefix with no pool after it — a key with a pool in it would name one cable per pool for one fact
the key is what the cable WOULD be named, and nothing is drawn for it: no name is the operator's absence, not a cable to nowhere. `wired` is the fact the drawing asks

dot.why: the cable is pulled from it, as from a pool row's output; the block's row stands where a pool card's row stands, so its dots are the same dots

the absence named out loud rather than left as a hole: nothing is pulled INTO a reader row, because a reader is the wiring the operator named, not a path a request runs through. A module that drew an input dot here would let a cable be dragged the wrong way and would read as if a request ran through the block

block.why: a name stands: the block holds the name the board gave, which is a fact about the name and not the answer the row got

the negative case, and the one the block always has a word for: no name is the operator's absence, and the block is drawn anyway, because a board that has no reader still has to say which absence it is. A block that drew nothing here would leave the absence as a hole, and its state would have to be invented from what pools exist — a fact read a second way

column.why: the order the column is read in: first who is called without a pool, then which model reads a picture for the board, then the pools themselves. Nothing here pins itself — Direct is the first block, not one held in view while the column scrolls (the owner, 2026-11-06), so a part has no position of its own and the order is the only fact about where it sits. The order is said once, in `poolsHtml`, and pinned by scripts/test_js_pool_board.py

the same order with one part named as not drawn: no pools, so no cards. The block is drawn even here, because the reader is the board's fact and not a pool's — its row says the absence in words. A part not drawn is still named here, because the order is a rule and not a drawing: a table that only listed what stands cannot say which part is missing

save.why: the reader is the board's, so the body names the board's field and nothing else: `ReaderBlock.body` says the shape once, and the door reads the body under `reader` — the same word `EntryModels::READER_FIELD` names for the file
the absence a click on the cable writes back: nothing named is sent as nothing, not as an empty name, so the wiring stays the absence it is

the negative case: a body that names no reader is not an empty name, and the door says what it reads — nothing named, which is the operator's absence, and the answer that writes it is `Reader::Nothing`. The page cannot build this body by hand — that is what `ReaderBlock.body` is for — and the guard holds the page and the door to the same key, so they cannot part

flow.why: a request that a reader read names the reader that read it, and that is the only thing that can light the row: the request says what it went through. The proxy writes `readerName` when the board's reader read the request's pictures for the row that serves it (rust/crates/proxy/src/exchange/reading.rs)

the reader is not the row that serves: a request that was read and then answered by a text row goes by both, and the drawing shows both. The reader key names the board's cable, not this pool's — one board, one reader

the negative case: a cable drawn is not a request that ran. Nothing lights the reader row until the request names who read its picture — a request whose row read the picture itself, or that carried none, names nobody. A row that lit because a cable was drawn would be a blink the board invented

a model called straight is read for too, when it cannot read the picture and the board's reader can: its way is the «Напрямую» row, and the reader's cable is the board's one cable, so the request lights both
no client to light: a reader key without its client's would be a cable whose other end is nobody

the reader's own request: it runs through the reader's cable and nothing else of the board — its client did not name the reader's pool, and lighting the client's cable to it would draw a request the client never sent
a reader that is a model called straight: its request lights the reader's cable alone, not the client's «Напрямую» row to that model
